caveats: Budgets are 'a brake, not a wall' (author-admitted): with a non-enforcing agent and no timeout, one runaway step can overshoot every cap unbounded and the loop only warns once (loop.py:3039-3082) — wind-down advisories cannot guarantee an ending actually happens.
Armed caps over fully-untracked spend can never trip; guards degrade to a one-time disclosure — any adopted detector must expect 'could not measure' states and disclose them rather than stay silent.

Squash-style condensation loses per-item ancestry: a resolution applied at the target is silently re-staged from the source on the next merge 'without a conflict to warn you' (author-admitted) — consolidation-level corrections resurface unless written back to source entries.

Heal-on-proof rests on Fractal's one-loop-per-node exclusivity, which Clauderizer lacks across hosts — its stranded-state detector must stay evidence-graded and advisory or it will false-strand live sessions ('a shell without tmux visibility must not kill a healthy loop').

Fractal's headline results (187-node self-audit, 135 issues/55 fixed, 698-to-823 tests, ten-for-ten blind validation, 17-kept/9-rejected defaults matrix) exist only as marketing narrative — grep over the full repo finds none of these numbers as inspectable artifacts; adopt mechanisms on code/doc evidence, not claimed outcomes.

Third-party validation is negligible: Show HN at 14 points with one content-free comment, a second post at 3 points/0 comments, docs.plasma.ai returning 403 — the only substantive external signal is three GitHub issues from real users, all without maintainer reply.

Issue #9 is an open, unanswered production-corruption report against the merge topology (unedited files silently regressed; another node's task contract spliced into a live NODE.md system prompt) — the two-speed-consolidation idea imports a pattern from a system whose own integration boundary demonstrably corrupted memory identity; adopt it with the merge-integrity audit, not instead of it.

Capability degradation in Fractal was discovered by users at runtime, not by its tests (hard tmux coupling in #3, undocumented out-of-worktree write paths in #6) — the parity-matrix half of the enforcement-ladder idea is the fix Fractal itself lacks, not something it proved.

Fractal's autonomy posture disables every backend's permission prompts and isolates only the branch, 'not the filesystem, the network, or anything else' (README warning) — its trust assumptions must not travel with its mechanisms.

Several admired disciplines are guidance-only even inside Fractal (child-sizing floor, commissioning gate 'is social — nothing in the tool enforces it') — they are design intentions, not validated enforcement, so citing them as proven practice overstates.

Infrastructure roughness behind the polished doctrine: the radio layer states 'strict atomicity is intentionally not provided' (documented four times) with unenforced message sizes; the SQLite schema is 'rebuilt, never migrated in place'; the instants ledger has admitted ambiguities (a healed pre-launch row is indistinguishable from a pre-stream death; cost on active rows is provisional).

Surfacing systems accrete measured token costs: the outbox backlog tax (~half a new worker's first-iteration budget, growing with spawn order) is the price Clauderizer's digest already pays in miniature — the receipts idea is the mitigation, not a free lunch, and its receipts table itself grows without bound.

assessment.fit_summary: Strong fit — this is a translation, not a transplant, and most of the translation is already free. Fractal's live-re-read machinery (core/loop.py:858-870, warn-and-keep) costs Clauderizer nothing: every cz_* call is a stateless re-read of canonical markdown, so a mid-flight budget retune lands at the next tool call by construction (INVARIANT-01 native). Fractal's "goal-met finish during wind-down still books completed" (RESERVE.md, design/budgets.md) is already true by construction: cz_transition_phase(complete) consults no gates and never blocks (INVARIANT-05 native). Fractal's kill-at-ceiling becomes a latched advisory state riding the existing conditional-digest-line + advisories-list plumbing. The one genuinely NEW mechanism Clauderizer must grow is an honest recorded-never-estimated spend unit — Fractal's own constitution (design/budgets.md: "spend is recorded, never estimated"; NULL ≠ $0) forbids token-estimation hacks, and Clauderizer cannot see host token usage, so spend must be work stints recorded by a blessed op (cz_preflight, which the procedure already mandates per work session). That ledger is the honest 20% of the work and the main empirical risk. The idea directly addresses a failure mode this repo has already paid for and instrumented reactively (memory-lag H-22; pre_compact); this makes the detector prospective instead of forensic. D-069-clean (the reserve assessor IS the executable detector), D-013-clean (assessed from disposable telemetry + canonical markdown, never an authority), and dormant-by-default (no declaration → zero bytes changed → INVARIANT-07/08 safe).

assessment.implementation_sketch: Alpha in four commits, all inside existing patterns. (1) telemetry.record_stint + preflight append (~25 lines): the ledger first, because everything else reads it; stint = {kind:'stint', date, gameplan, phase, proc:PROC_TAG}; PROC_TAG = uuid4().hex[:8] at telemetry import (one MCP server process = one session). (2) rituals/budgets.py (~150 lines): _GP_BUDGET_RE = r'^>\s*Budget:\s*(\d+)\s*(sessions?|iterations/session)' over the GAMEPLAN.md header; _PHASE_BUDGET_RE = r'^\*\*Budget\*\*:\s*(\d+)\s*sessions?' inside phase_block(); spent(gid, phase) = len({e['proc'] for e in read_events if e.kind=='stint' and match}) with distinct-date fallback when proc is absent (forward-compat); assess() emits per-tier state: 'untracked' when budget declared but zero stints AND phase in_progress (Fractal's NULL-honesty: never claim '0 spent, all remaining'); wind_down when spent >= budget - reserve and spent >= 1; over when spent > budget. The latch needs no stored state: spend is append-only-monotone and the budget re-reads live, so wind_down is sticky until the human raises the number in markdown — which IS the sanctioned retune. (3) surfacing (~45 lines total): bundle['budgets'] in compute(); one conditional digest line; wind_down attachment in cz_next_phase_context, cz_loop_step, preflight result, pre_compact. Advisory text verbatim-shared via budgets.describe() (the L-55 one-wording seam memory_lag.describe follows). (4) docs + template + tests. Explicitly OUT of alpha: any token/cost estimation (violates recorded-never-estimated), any block or config flag, per-step leashes (no Clauderizer analogue — the host owns execution), auto-running any Ending Protocol op.

INTEGRATION — (f) cz_preflight appends exactly one well-formed stint line, append-only (prior telemetry bytes untouched — INVARIANT-03 pattern from test_telemetry.py); (g) cz_status bundle carries 'budgets' iff declared; (h) render_digest byte-identical for the undeclared golden fixture (extend tests/test_back_compat_focus.py::test_single_gameplan_digest_is_byte_identical) and emits exactly one ⏳ line for a wind_down fixture; (i) cz_next_phase_context carries wind_down for a reserve-window phase; (j) cz_loop_step carries wind_down after N in-process calls against a declared iterations/session budget; (k) SOVEREIGNTY REGRESSION: cz_transition_phase(complete) during wind_down returns ok=True with zero budget-related refusal text (the INVARIANT-05 pin); (l) hook safety: compute(conditions=False) with budgets spawns no subprocess and writes nothing (pattern of test_compute_default_never_evaluates_hook_safety), and read ops stay write-free (tests/test_read_only_ops.py).
assessment.empirical_verification: Per D-064, run the multi-agent/multi-session matrix (≥3 host legs: Claude Code/WSL, Kimi desktop, ops-mode CLI) on real gameplans with budgets declared vs matched gameplans without, over ≥2 weeks of dogfooding, and measure from durable evidence already emitted today — no new instrumentation: (1) PRIMARY: memory-lag firings per phase (rituals/memory_lag.py, the recorded signature of a session dying without landing state) and missing-handoff preflight findings — the claim is that phases whose sessions SAW a WIND_DOWN advisory produce measurably fewer of both; (2) landed-ending rate: fraction of phase completions whose handoff file + outputs + phase summary existed BEFORE the completing session ended (checkable from git history, the memory_lag anchor technique) with vs without the advisory; (3) calibration honesty: distribution of recorded stints vs declared budgets (if real phases routinely run 3x their declared sessions, the declaration grammar is fiction and the feature should not graduate); (4) recording coverage: fraction of work sessions that produced a stint at all (if agents skip preflight, spend under-records and the detector is structurally blind — measure this FIRST, it gates everything); (5) noise: dream notes (kind: friction/drift) referencing the wind-down line, and any observed case of an agent refusing legitimate new work because of the advisory (the over-obedience failure). Graduation gate: the template's `> Budget:` suggestion ships as a default only after (1)/(2) improve across at least two host legs and (5) shows no over-obedience incident; until then the mechanism ships dormant (undeclared repos see zero bytes changed).
risks: Spend-proxy validity is the load-bearing risk: stint = cz_preflight run assumes the procedure is followed, but agents skipping preflight is exactly the discipline failure this system fights — under-recorded spend makes the reserve latch structurally blind (fires never), and the feature silently becomes decoration. Measure recording coverage first (D-064 item 4) and keep NULL-honesty phrasing so 'no stints recorded' is never read as 'budget untouched'.

Over-obedience: agents demonstrably treat advisories as gates; a mis-declared budget latching wind_down early could make an agent refuse legitimate work on a healthy phase. The advisory text must always carry the sovereignty clause and the retune path (raise Budget: in GAMEPLAN.md), and the D-064 matrix must actively look for refusal incidents.

Session identity is fuzzy across hosts: the per-process tag equates one MCP server process with one session, but `clauderize ops` spawns a fresh process per batch (overcounts) and a mid-session server restart splits one session in two; multi-window same-repo work (the H-05 world) blurs it further. Acceptable only because the output is advisory — never present counts as authoritative sessions, always as 'recorded stints'.

Digest regression risk (INVARIANT-08): every conditional line added to render_digest has historically needed byte-identity care; the frozen golden test protects the undeclared path, but the declared path adds a recurring line to every status of a wind-down phase — cap it at ONE line and re-check the handoff token gauge doesn't inflate.

Scope-creep toward enforcement: Fractal's per-step leash and cost ceilings have no honest Clauderizer analogue (the engine cannot see tokens or spend), and the tempting shortcut — estimating session capacity from context size or call counts — violates the recorded-never-estimated premise the idea itself cites. The alpha boundary (two-and-a-half tiers, stints only, advisory only) must be pinned in the procedure doc as deliberate.

Telemetry constitution widening: adding a third blessed writer (preflight) and a new event kind is small but touches an append-only file other readers (corpus_health, curate, lesson_health) parse — they filter by kind so unknown kinds pass through, but this must be asserted, not assumed (one test: existing curators ignore stint events byte-for-byte).

idea.name: honest-terminal-vocabulary
idea.what: A close-out vocabulary that cannot launder: completed = goal-met only, declared by the agent while alive with criteria verified; exited = designed stop short of goal (budget/scope/session exhausted — resumable, 'inspect the work', not failed); abnormal end distinct; a container (gameplan) never 'fails' — failure is recorded on the phase/item that failed. Classification is order-independent and fails closed (unreadable evidence reclassifies toward exited, never open into completed). Engine-authored reason strings use a reserved machine-classifiable grammar (stem + figures; cascades carry a '(via <entity>)' attribution suffix) matched in full so agent free text cannot spoof engine classifications, and agents are told to phrase reasons in their own words. Clauderizer shape: three-way vocabulary on cz_transition_phase/close-gameplan plus a D-069 detector surfacing 'this close-out would launder unmet exit criteria into a clean completion' as an advisory finding.
idea.evidence: wiki/design/statuses.md:44-84 ('status carries the nuance, the exit code carries the alarm'); loop.py:3398-3432 (anti-shadowing: 'completed would launder a dead iteration into a clean run'), 3271-3354 (order-independent, fail-closed), 63-75 + 3748-3764 (reserved reason stems, full-shape matching); RESERVE.md:26-30 ('write your reason in your own words'); NODE.md:56-64; wiki/user_flow/finishing.md. Four readers converged on the same mechanism.
idea.why_for_clauderizer: Clauderizer phases share one 'done' door, so the next session cannot tell scope-cut from goal-met in a handoff. Advisory laundering detector satisfies INVARIANT-05; 'completed carries the evidence-bearing reason' operationalizes D-012; the reserved engine grammar keeps dreamer/curator/cascade parsers sound over append-only history (INVARIANT-03) and gives cascade records a propagation-surviving attribution pattern.

assessment.empirical_verification: Per D-064, evidence from a multi-agent matrix (Claude Code plus at least one non-Claude host, >=2 repos, >=10 sessions), not one session. Three measurable signals: (1) False-green claim rate — count sessions where the preflight verdict was PASS WITH WARNINGS with gates_unrun non-empty, then check whether the session's handoff/close-out text claims "tests pass"; success = that claim rate drops versus baseline transcripts where the same condition was only a skip-count in a summary string. (2) Time-to-detection of a dead guard — seed a deliberately erroring standing-condition probe in a loop gameplan and run 3+ sessions per agent; baseline is effectively never (both surfaces hide the failure today); success = the "cannot trip" disclosure is acknowledged (probe fixed or condition removed) within the first session that evaluates conditions. (3) Dormancy misprioritization — pause a repo 30+ calendar days with ~2 active days, resume across the matrix, and compare whether agents treat the stale-findings digest nag as "old backlog to deprioritize" (baseline distortion) versus correctly reading working time from the active-days disclosure, measured from next_action choices and handoff text. Secondary: on fresh clones (no telemetry), zero curator proposals contain a numeric ranking claim over an unmeasured lesson (grep the proposals JSON across matrix runs).
risks: Digest/advisory fatigue: a 'cannot trip' warning that fires on a transient probe timeout (one 30s blip on a loaded machine) trains agents to ignore it — mitigate by disclosing only in tool paths (preflight / cz_status conditions=True), which already never run in the hook, and consider requiring the same probe to fail twice before the digest line (adds state — start without it).

git-derived active-days is itself a fallible reading: shallow clones, squash merges, and rebases undercount distinct commit dates, so the working-time figure could be the new false claim — keep it hedged ('~N active day(s)'), keep the 30d threshold on calendar days, and never flip the threshold basis without D-064 matrix evidence.

Back-compat of external consumers: flipping conditions' met to tri-state None would break `if c.get("met")` truthiness in any clauderize-ops JSON reader — the sketch deliberately uses an additive `unevaluable` field instead; similarly preflight adds `verdict`/`gates_unrun` rather than changing `passed` (INVARIANT-07).

Vocabulary drift (L-65 seam): 'unknown' joins the preflight status set that README/procedure prose and the digest renderer enumerate — without the pin test the surfaces drift silently, exactly the class L-65 documents.

Behavior change on hung suites: today a 600s TimeoutExpired crashes the tool call loudly; containment turns it into a polite 'unknown' — arguably a quieter signal for a serious problem; mitigated by the PASS WITH WARNINGS verdict and the explicit 'UNKNOWN, not pass' wording, but worth watching in the matrix.

Scope creep toward transplant: the storage half is already native, and the tempting next step (a pause/resume event log on gameplans to credit back DEFERRED spans precisely) would add new stored state and enforcement-adjacent deadline semantics Clauderizer has no consumer for — resist until a real reader needs it.

The idea fills a measured gap: D-068 mandates surface-by-relevance-drop-nothing, but the open-findings/open-items digest lines have no relevance axis at all — every unresolved id re-bills every session identically, which is precisely fractal's measured outbox tax (new-subscriber backlog read = new agent's first cz_status on a repo with a deep open register). assessment.empirical_verification: Per D-064 (DECISIONS.md:479 — multi-agent matrix, never one session): run a matrix of at least 2 hosts (claude-code hook host + one hook-less host, e.g. codex or cursor via MCP bootstrap) x 3+ consecutive real sessions each, on a repo seeded with 5+ open findings/items, with two DIFFERENT reader agents interleaved on the same checkout. Measurable signals, all from existing instrumentation plus the new sidecar: (A) per-reader isolation — after agent A cz_gets three findings, agent B's next digest still foregrounds all five as unseen when split per-reader (fractal's 'your receipts never move another node's unread view'), while A's backgrounds three; (B) engagement latency — sessions-until-first-receipt per finding (finding date vs first seen line), compared before/after: the foregrounded never-seen set should shorten a NEW agent's time-to-engagement on its first session (the directed version of fractal's measured new-subscriber backlog tax, ~half a first-iteration budget); (C) acknowledged-vs-ignored rate — fraction of open findings with >=1 receipt after the matrix; the corpus_health never-engaged advisory must fire on a finding every session ignored and stay quiet on engaged ones (D-069 detector proven on live behavior); (D) drop-nothing audit — diff cz_list_findings/cz_list_open_items output before vs after: identical sets every session (receipts changed labeling only). Ship the default only if (A) and (D) hold in every matrix cell and (B) or (C) shows at least one real behavior change (an agent engaging a foregrounded item it had ignored across prior sessions).
risks: Digest-shape churn: the open-findings/open-items lines are golden-tested and habit-forming; the unseen/seen split must add zero bytes when no receipts exist or it breaks the D6 byte-identical gate and the INVARIANT-08 conditional-emission discipline — the first receipt ever written permanently changes digest shape for that machine, which reviewers should accept knowingly.

Read-op purity erosion: cz_get is documented read-only with no write lock (L-03, ops.py:178); writing receipts from it stretches the disposable-cache precedent (ops.py:183-185) — must stay lock-free O_APPEND single-line writes with a torn-line-tolerant reader, and test_read_only_ops.py's _DISPOSABLE edit must be scoped to exactly the one filename.

False 'seen': via='handoff'/'phase_context' receipts claim the agent saw ids whose bodies rode in a bundle it may never have attended to — over-backgrounding a critical finding. Mitigated because backgrounding is labeling-only (ids never leave the digest) and the findings_age staleness warning fires regardless of seen state; a stricter alpha could receipt only via cz_get/resolve.

Per-machine blindness: the gitignored sidecar means machine B inherits no receipts from machine A — correct per-reader semantics (and D-067's classification), but users may expect team-wide seen state; needs the same explicit 'personal, not team' framing D-052 gave dismissals.

Sidecar growth: receipts written per-handoff every session grow the JSONL; idempotent-per-(id,reader) writes bound it to O(open items x readers) in steady state, but a pathological loop of new findings still grows it — acceptable for a gitignored disposable file, worth a doctor line if it ever exceeds a few MB.

Concurrent same-machine writers: two agents appending simultaneously can interleave or duplicate lines — same exposure class D-067 already accepts for telemetry.jsonl; the tolerant reader plus advisory semantics make the worst case a re-foregrounded item, never lost canonical state.

Per-user ledger vs team-shared judgment: dismissing a false-positive pair in .clauderizer/proposals.local.toml (gitignored, D-052) suppresses it on one machine only, so converged differs across clones; must report suppressed_count in every summary (the D-063/D-065 lesson — a suppressed state must never present as a clean one), and a later 2.0 step may want the shared markdown form (the not_related_to precedent) instead.

Merge-base must suppress re-proposing, never re-judging: if the filter becomes authority (no way to see suppressed proposals), it violates the D-013 pointer-not-authority spirit — keep an include-suppressed read path.

idea.name: merge-integrity-audit-for-canonical-docs
idea.what: An advisory detector auditing git merges that touch docs/: diff which tracked entities/files the merge actually changed against what writer.py audit trails legitimately edited, and surface unexplained doc reverts, foreign-gameplan frontmatter collisions, conflict-marker leakage, or infra-file bleed-through as findings. Grounded in Fractal's one real production failure (open issue, no maintainer reply): squash merges with no merge-base record silently regressed files the node never edited (an 88-line README reverted to pre-fork state), and raw conflict markers spliced 'another node's task contract' into a live NODE.md system prompt — memory-identity corruption mid-run. Fractal enforces scope at commit time but not merge time; the gap is the bug.
idea.evidence: github.com/plasma-ai/fractal/issues/9 (verbatim production failure report from user nealxpatel); wiki/design/commit_discipline.md:45-50 in-clone (scope enforced at commit only, confirming the merge-time gap). The only candidate backed by an observed third-party failure rather than design intent.
idea.why_for_clauderizer: Clauderizer's canon is markdown merged through ordinary git; multi-worktree/multi-agent use (cz_assign, D-064 matrix runs) has exactly this hazard — a merge silently regressing decisions/handoffs or splicing one gameplan's context into another. INVARIANT-05 shape: surface the anomaly for judgment, never block the merge; INVARIANT-02 supplies ground truth, since writer.py knows what was legitimately edited.

assessment.fit_summary: Strong fit, with one required correction to the idea as stated. Clauderizer's canon is markdown merged through ordinary git; its own procedure names merge hazards in prose (GAMEPLAN-PROCEDURE.md:988-1030) with zero executable check, and D-069 rules that a discipline without a detector is a defect. The proven in-repo template already exists: memory_lag.py is a read-only, bounded, exception-swallowing, git-evidence advisory detector surfaced conditionally in digest + preflight — the merge audit is that same shape pointed at merge commits. Fractal's enforcement (commit refusal, RuntimeError on markers in fractal/core/node.py and its wiki lint) translates cleanly to advisory surfacing per INVARIANT-05: same evidence, findings instead of blocks. The correction: Clauderizer has no 'writer.py audit trail' (revision.json is explicitly not an audit log, revision.py:19), and a machine-local write journal could never explain a teammate's merge anyway — so the ground truth becomes git itself (merge parents + merge-base blob comparison), which is also the only machine-SHARED evidence and therefore the correct choice under D-064's multi-agent frame. Honest scope cost to state up front: the headline Fractal failure (issue #9) was a SQUASH merge, which leaves no second parent — the parent-based revert detector cannot see squashes; the conflict-marker and duplicate-id classes still catch squash damage, and the module must state this blind spot the way memory_lag.py states its in_progress one (D-012 honesty).

changes.change: The detector module, modeled on memory_lag.py's discipline (read-only, _GIT_TIMEOUT-bounded subprocess, never raises, silent when healthy): (a) conflict-marker triad scan over tracked docs/*.md — requires the full '<<<<<<< '/'======='/'>>>>>>> ' sequence so a lone setext '=======' underline never fires; (b) latest merge commit touching docs_rel via `git log --merges -n 1 --format=%H %P -- <docs_rel>`; (c) revert detection: for merge M with parents P1 P2, base = merge-base(P1,P2); flag paths where blob(M,f)==blob(base,f)!=blob(P1,f) AND blob(HEAD,f) still ==blob(base,f) — self-clearing when repaired, no persisted flag (D-069 rule 3, D-065); (d) .clauderizer bleed-through attribution via `git diff --name-only P1 M -- .clauderizer`; (e) shared describe() one-liners (L-55 seam).

Add _merge_signals(paths) alongside _git_signals; findings join the audit dict, finding_count, and summary — cz_audit is the gameplan-close gate and phase-merge damage should surface there. Advisory list entries only; no blocking, no config flag (INVARIANT-05).

In compute(), after the memory_lag block: try/except-guarded bundle['merge_integrity'] = merge_audit.detect(paths), set only when non-None. In render_digest(): one conditional '⚠ Merge integrity: …' line, zero bytes when absent (INVARIANT-08; a healthy repo's digest stays byte-identical, INVARIANT-07).

check_merge_integrity() mirroring check_memory_lag (preflight.py:527-546): appended only when findings exist, level 'warn' never 'fail' (D-024 keeps blocking for preflight's OWN checks; this is a discipline advisory).

No new tool for alpha — surfaces through existing cz_audit / cz_preflight / cz_status, keeping MCP tool-description token cost flat (the D-064 cross-model routing concern). Extend cz_audit's docstring to name the merge signals.

assessment.implementation_sketch: One new ritual module + three small wiring diffs; writer.py and mutations untouched (INVARIANT-02 unaffected — this is a pure reader). merge_audit.py (~150-200 lines): `_git(root,*args)` copied from memory_lag.py:55-63 (never raises, 10s timeout, broken git = no evidence, INVARIANT-04/06); `marker_findings(paths)` globs paths.docs.rglob('*.md') and scans line-wise for the state-machine triad, returning [{path, line}] — always-on because a leaked marker in canonical memory is a defect however it arrived (the Fractal NODE.md-corruption class); `latest_docs_merge(paths)` returns {sha, parents[]} or None from `git log --merges -n 1 --format='%H %P' -- <docs_rel>` (docs_rel derived exactly as memory_lag._owned_prefixes does, so custom docs roots work); `regressions(paths, merge)` computes base via `git merge-base P1 P2`, candidates via `git diff --name-only P1 M -- <docs_rel>`, then compares blob ids from `git rev-parse <commit>:<path>` — a path is flagged only while M:path==base:path!=P1:path and HEAD:path==base:path, so restoring the lost content retires the finding from evidence alone (no persisted state, D-065/D-069); `infra(paths, merge)` = `git diff --name-only P1 M -- .clauderizer`; `detect(paths)` assembles {markers, merge:{sha, short, regressions, infra}} or None when all empty; `describe()` renders the one-line claims ('merge a1b2c3d reverted docs/DECISIONS.md to its pre-fork state — P1's changes are gone from HEAD; restore or affirm intentional'). Duplicate-id collision attribution is NOT rebuilt — _graph_integrity already reports collisions in every corpus_health/status read; the digest line simply sits beside it. Module docstring states the squash blind spot plainly, mirroring memory_lag.py:25-28's honest-cost paragraph. Everything advisory: no block, no enable/disable flag, agent judges every finding (INVARIANT-05).
assessment.test_plan: tests/test_merge_audit.py, conventions from tests/test_memory_lag.py (local _git_repo/_commit helpers over the temp_repo fixture; no network; deterministic). Both-direction proofs per L-25: (1) markers planted in docs/DECISIONS.md are found with path+line; (2) a legitimate setext '=======' underline alone stays silent (false-positive direction); (3) a two-branch repo where the merge resolution restores the pre-fork blob of docs/VISION.md fires a regression finding naming the file and merge sha; (4) a clean non-overlapping merge yields detect()==None and the rendered digest is byte-identical to the no-merge digest (INVARIANT-07/08); (5) re-committing the lost content after the bad merge retires the finding with no state file written (assert .clauderizer gained no new files); (6) a squash merge that splices markers still fires the marker class — and detect() carries no false revert claim for it; (7) a merge bringing .clauderizer/revision.json changes is attributed as infra bleed-through; (8) preflight appends check 'merge_integrity' at level 'warn' never 'fail', and appends nothing on a healthy repo; (9) cz_audit result includes the merge list and cz_audit stays registered writes=False (mirror of tests/test_audit.py:81); (10) non-git directory and git-timeout paths return None, never raise (hook safety). Integration: run the full existing suite (~1253 tests) to prove digest/preflight byte-identity holds everywhere else.
assessment.empirical_verification: Per D-064 the evidence must come from the multi-agent matrix, not one session — and this feature is idle by construction on a single-branch repo, so single-session evidence is impossible anyway. Concrete protocol: extend the existing two-branch concurrency probe (the one whose revision.json merge-conflict evidence is cited in docs/DECISIONS.md:506-509) to N>=2 agents in separate worktrees of one clauderized repo, each writing decisions/lessons/handoffs via cz_* on its branch, then integrating via both true merges and squash merges. Measure three named signals: (a) seeded-fault detection rate — of K injected merge faults (an ours-revert of DECISIONS.md, a conflict-marker splice into a handoff, a .clauderizer file riding the merge), the fraction surfaced in the NEXT session's digest/preflight BEFORE any agent read the corrupted memory (target: 3/3 for true merges; markers+infra classes for squashes, with the revert miss recorded as the known blind spot); (b) clean-merge false-positive rate — across M>=10 clean multi-agent merges, zero findings and byte-identical digests; (c) at least one ORGANIC catch during real matrix dogfooding on this repo (its own gameplan workflows already run multi-agent worktree fans), recorded as a finding with the merge sha as evidence. The headline metric: corrupted-memory sessions prevented — a session that would have loaded a silently reverted decision log or a marker-spliced handoff (Fractal issue #9's exact failure, memory-identity corruption mid-run) receives the warning first.
risks: Squash merges — the exact mechanism of the motivating Fractal failure — defeat the parent-based revert detector (no second parent, no merge-base record); only the marker and infra classes cover them, so the feature must state this blind spot in its docstring and digest wording or it over-claims (D-012).

False positives on intentional reverts: an agent may legitimately resolve a merge back to base; the advisory framing and self-clearing retirement mitigate, but a wolf-crying digest line erodes trust in all advisories — the clean-merge byte-identity tests and matrix false-positive measurement are the guard.

Hook-path latency: detect() adds several bounded git subprocesses (log --merges, merge-base, per-file rev-parse) to status_bundle.compute(), which SessionStart hooks call; must cap at the single most recent docs-touching merge and reuse the 10s timeout, else session start slows on big repos.

Marker-scan precision: docs that QUOTE conflict markers (a lesson about this very feature would) can trip the triad scan; per-file findings with line numbers keep it judgeable, but the corpus of this repo itself may need the finding affirmed-and-ignored occasionally.

Single-author idleness: on repos with no merges the detector never fires, so its value cannot be proven from this repo's own history (D-064's single-author caveat) — shipping it as a load-bearing claim before the matrix evidence lands would repeat the D-062 mistake.

Windows/CI git variance: rev-parse blob comparisons and merge-base behavior must hold on windows-latest cells (the write_atomic O-01 history shows platform surprises are real here); the never-raises _git wrapper contains the blast radius but silent no-evidence returns must not be read as a pass (D-065).
